title: Is AI stealing Gen Z’s first job?
caption:
Two serious studies seem to disagree on whether AI is taking Gen Z's first jobs.

Stanford's Digital Economy Lab reported Aug 12 that employment of 22- to 25-year-olds in the most AI-exposed jobs is 19% below where it would be had it matched peers in less-exposed jobs. A year ago the gap was 15%.

UCLA economists then checked recent grads. Unemployment this summer was about 7%, normal for recent years, with no significant AI effect.

Both can be true. In AI-exposed jobs, juniors aren't being laid off; fewer are being hired. ZipRecruiter says entry-level jobs fell to 38.6% of postings in March, from 44% in 2023.

On Oct 2, BLS said unemployment for 20- to 24-year-olds jumped to 8.0% in September, from 7.1% in August, though it's down from 9.2% a year ago. One month is noisy, and neither study proves AI is the cause.

Our take: the ladder is the asset. Cutting junior hiring saves money this year and costs you every senior you'd have had in 2035. The work AI does first is the work juniors learn on. Hire them anyway.

On the record, Oct 3, 2026: By Dec 31, 2027, the latest Stanford Digital Economy Lab update puts the gap for 22- to 25-year-olds in the most AI-exposed jobs above 19%.

Every senior was a junior someone took a chance on.

Who took a chance on you? Who are you taking one on?
